content_preview.title: Linux 7.4-rc1 Drops the Assisted-by Tag From Docs; Torvalds Says AI Fixes Drove Much of rc2, Where 11.5% of Non-Merge Commits Carry It (Herald Count)
content_preview.summary: The kernel's Assisted-by tag, on about 10% of non-merge commits through 7.3-rc7 per LWN, left the docs in 7.4-rc1. Torvalds says AI fixes drove much of rc2; a Herald count finds the tag on 105 of 913 non-merge commits since rc1, a floor that misses undisclosed use.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

The Linux kernel's documentation asked contributors to mark patches written with LLM help with an `Assisted-by:` line in the commit message. According to [LWN](https://lwn.net/Articles/1099594/), `Documentation/process/coding-assistants.rst` "was added to the 7.0 kernel" and calls for the tag "to be added to the changelog of patches developed with LLM assistance". The [commit that later removed the tag](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/1e035297ffdadf2184c3c773b8c098e372324...

recommendations: Publish with the filed corrections record.
State the counting rule exactly as run (case-insensitive, leading whitespace allowed) or use the strict rule and its figures.
Link the earlier 2026-10/21 Analysis, which reported the consensus at the Maintainers Summit.

editor_notes.content_quality: Original measurement Analysis (about 1,531 words; Background, Current situation, Implications) that follows up the Herald's 2026-10/21 Analysis, which could not say whether the removal had been merged. Primary records (the removal commit, the docs pull, the docs pages), LWN, Phoronix and Linuxiac are kept apart from the Herald's own counts, which are labelled and described. The Implications section is explicitly labelled as analysis, treats the count as a floor, and declines to claim the table confirms or contradicts Torvalds.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 11 snapshots (source-0 to source-10); every sha256 matches the manifest and every status is 200. Four Phoronix pages (source-3 to source-6) are Archive.org fallback captures (timestamps 20261113121627, 20261112152048, 20261023072703, 20261112201928); live Phoronix returns a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403) for me too, as the article says. Quotes: all 28 quoted spans in the body matched by script against the snapshots (LWN, the removal commit, the docs pull, the docs pages, three Phoronix reports and Linuxiac); Torvalds's rc2 and rc1 passages, the 'AI normal' phrase (Torvalds's own wording in the rc6 announcement as Phoronix quotes it), the Coccinelle and LTS statements and Linuxiac's 'didn't say which of the AI tools' sentence are all on the pages attributed. GitHub API: removal commit 1e035297ff authored by Sasha Levin 2026-10-13T12:15:01Z and committed by Jonathan Corbet 2026-10-14T16:51:49Z, with the files and message the article describes; docs-7.4 pull 14c8977 committed 2026-10-21T00:38:38Z (raw commit author/committer timestamp 1792543118 with offset -1000, i.e. October 20 in UTC-10:00); git merge-base: the removal commit is an ancestor of v7.4-rc1 and not of v7.3. docs.kernel.org coding-assistants and generated-content pages show 7.4.0-rc2 and contain no 'Assisted-by'. Herald counts reproduced from a filtered clone of torvalds/linux with tags v7.2 to v7.4-rc2: non-merge commits per interval 15,267; 615; 651; 523; 577; 535; 365; 232; 18,591; 913 all match; merge-inclusive 16,267 (7.3 window, equals Phoronix's table value) and 990 (rc1 to rc2, equals the GitHub compare view); v7.2..v7.3-rc7 is 18,533 non-merge commits (equals LWN and the commit message); the Fixes: proxy figures (508 of 3,402; 1,233 of 4,932; 90 of 742) and '51 of 105 carry exactly Assisted-by: LLM' reproduce exactly (the rc1 to rc2 interval also via the GitHub compare API: 990 commits, 913 non-merge, 105 tagged). Tagged counts: the article's 1,258 (7.3 window), 3,008 (7.4 window) and 1,877 (through 7.3-rc7) are each one higher than the stated rule gives (1,257; 3,007; 1,876): the published figures also match an indented 'Assisted-by: LLM' line in documentation commit 816d9992d9ed ('coding-assistants: simplify attribution', which quotes the tag as an example) and one commit that writes 'Assisted-By:' (4e7c4a59a533, an iwlwifi patch); shares at one decimal are unchanged and the headline interval (105 of 913, 11.5%) is unaffected. Independence: LWN (one article), Phoronix (four articles count once) and Linuxiac, 3 outlets; LWN's author is also the removal commit's committer, which the article says, so Phoronix and Linuxiac are the outlets independent of the commit; the commits and docs pages are subject pages. Anthropic disclosure: not required - neither the article nor any passage it cites mentions Anthropic or Claude (hits in snapshots are one LWN reader comment and a Phoronix sidebar headline; the kernel history has a commit crediting a Claude model, which the article does not mention). Scanner: no flags.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No wrong statement in the headline, summary or lead. Subordinate: (1) the counting rule stated in the article differs from the rule that produces its tagged counts, leaving three counts one too high and the 'seven fewer than LWN's 1,884' figure one short (eight under the stated rule); filed as a correction. (2) The article quotes LWN's 'a strong consensus in the room' but omits the removal commit's 'strong, though not unanimous' wording and LWN's report that Khan said she still found the tag useful; filed as a clarification. Verified correct: dates and time zones, the 7.3 and 7.4 figures, LWN's 18,533 and 1,884, Torvalds's statements and the BPF attribution (Alexei Starovoitov per Linuxiac, Torvalds relaying 'Alexei claims').
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive; the Herald's own counts are labelled and caveated as a floor; no claim that the table confirms Torvalds.
editor_notes.originality: Follow-up with new information (the removal is merged and present in v7.4-rc1) and new data (the Herald's per-interval counts). The linked 2026-10/21 Analysis exists and its corrections (COSMIC timing, GCC marking condition) concern other passages and are not repeated. No other published article reports these counts.
concerns: Phoronix's 7.3-rc6 page body says 'rc7' in its first sentence while its headline and the Torvalds quotation say rc6; the article follows the headline and the announcement label.
The rc1 to rc2 comparison rests on one interval; the article says so.
The Herald's tag count is a floor on disclosure and also counts only commit messages; the article says so.
recommendations: State the counting rule as run.
Mention the dissent reported by LWN.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Careful, well-sourced Analysis with original measurement that meets the Analysis requirements (about 1,531 words, 11 sources, 3 independent outlets counted per outlet, facts separated from analysis) and whose headline figure and quotations reproduce exactly. Approved with one correction (three tagged counts one too high) and one clarification. Featured candidacy: 2 - original, reproducible measurement of AI-assisted commit tagging in the Linux kernel with Torvalds's own statements, relevant to a broad developer audience though based on one interval and a disclosure floor
